outcome.answer: The closest match is a two-stage method combining structured supervised fine-tuning with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to detect polarization in social-media text. It trains the model to fill slots for the target, claim type, manifestations, and justification, then uses preference pairs to reduce false negatives [2]. This detects polarization rather than directly assigning each post a left–right political leaning. For political stance detection in informal posts, another paper improves classification by supplying summaries of users’ past posts as context, but does not describe slot-based training or preference optimization [1].
